newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds closed firmer in line with U.S. and German markets, helped by a firmer Swiss franc, declining interest rates and technical factors, dealers said.
"Everything that helps was there," one trader said, although activity was on the subdued side.
The average yield on government bonds fell three ticks to 3.13 percent, the lowest since March 1979.

Dealers said the biggest volume was in domestic bonds, especially in longer maturities. Market makers dominated the business with customers mostly on the sidelines, uncertain about the future direction.
Dealers expected prices to drift higher this week in the absence of unexpected news and with the sluggish Swiss economy unlikely to generate inflationary pressure.

On the grey market, BNG's new 12-year 3-5/8 percent bond priced at 102.50 percent was trading to yield 3.65 percent. Credit Suisse also announced a 12-year, four percent subordinated bond at par that was yielding 3.97 percent.
Other grey market prices were slightly higher.
